lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A season that once promised more now looks like a six-alarm fire - and Saturday's shutout only deepened the smoke. The Maple Leafs fell 1-0 to Edmonton, their sixth straight loss and fourth consecutive defeat, finishing a winless homestand with no goals to show for their best effort in days. Toronto is 8-12, 13th in the Eastern Conference, with 18 points and a 10-point gap to climb. The margin for error has vanished. Morgan Rielly remains sidelined with a lower-body injury, upgraded to day-to-day but still scratched, while Chris Tanev returned and immediately underscored the club's defensive strain. Connor McDavid's 50-point night and 21-game scoring streak belonged to Edmonton; Toronto's answer was silence. Tuesday's visit to Chicago at 7:30 p.m. ET on TSN is no mere change of scenery - it is the first test of whether this skid becomes a season's defining scar.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason has arrived with a blunt diagnosis: Toronto needs thunder, not another season of polite competence. The most important development is the Blue Jays' reported interest in Seiya Suzuki, a target who would bring power, reliability and a legitimate threat against left-handed pitching. That matters because the club's season is over, and its final points total was -2.0 - a number that should sharpen every decision this winter. Suzuki is the cleaner fit than another all-purpose outfielder; he could change the shape of an order that too often asked lesser bats to carry major weight. Toronto is also circling Ketel Marte, while the Japanese market's broader crop, from Teruaki Sato onward, deserves serious attention. The roster needs impact, not decoration. Watch whether the Jays turn that interest into a cornerstone bat before the March 25 opener at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors are wobbling toward another matchup with the Knicks, and the margin for error has narrowed to a sliver. Toronto's 123-112 loss to Philadelphia on Nov. 12 extended its skid to three games, leaving the club 5-7 and fourth in the Atlantic Division, five games behind. The offense has lost its organizer: Scottie Barnes, sidelined four games by a left groin strain, is questionable after taking part in Saturday's practice. That is the day's hinge. Kawhi Leonard remains out while progressing through individual on-court work, with no timetable, a familiar reminder that Toronto has yet to see its intended core settle. New York has become an unpleasant riddle for this group, and the Raptors cannot solve it with half a roster. Tonight's 6 p.m. meeting with the Knicks is less about a November rescue than whether Barnes can return and stop the slide before it hardens into the season's identity.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders are winning the small battles that keep a season alive, but they remain one bad Sunday from falling out of the picture. Washington's 24-21 victory over the Giants moved the club to 3-5-1, kept its winning streak at one, and left it third in the NFC East - two games back. Luke McCaffrey's clever out-of-bounds kickoff maneuver helped create the kind of field-position edge that decided a narrow game, while Jayden Daniels delivered the winning touchdown to Stefon Diggs when Washington needed its quarterback to make the moment matter. The margin remains thin: Lucas Patrick is out with a concussion, and Colson Yankoff is sidelined by a knee injury. The Giants may debate conservative play-calling, but Washington's job is simpler now - close the gap. Next comes Cincinnati on Nov. 23, with the Commanders needing another win to turn a flicker into a pursuit.

article.title: Maple Leafs Lose 1-0 to Oilers
paragraphs: The Maple Leafs finished a winless homestand with a 1-0 loss to Edmonton on Saturday. Anthony Stolarz stopped 22 shots, but Toronto could not solve Devon Levi. The Leafs next visit the Blackhawks Tuesday at 7:30 p.m. ET on TSN.

The Raptors host the Knicks today at 6 p.m. ET. Nate Bittle, Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard are listed out, while Kevin McCullar Jr. is day-to-day with an illness. Toronto enters at 5-7. The Blue Jays are looking ahead to a March 25 regular-season opener at the Yankees, with Japanese stars and limited power bats shaping the early offseason conversation.
The Commanders next face the Bengals on Monday, November 23. Toronto's next game starts at 6 p.m. at Scotiabank Arena.
